subject: Post-demo: recommended shortlist + cost/latency clarifications
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
To: Alex Morris <alex.morris@stratus.finance>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 31 May 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: recommended shortlist + next steps

Hi Alex / Priya —

Appreciate you carving out time today. Quick recap from our side and a recommended shortlist to move into a short pilot: 

TL;DR shortlist (attached benchmark + prompt pack):
- Option 1 — Redwood-3q-8B (quantized): best cost per token, good at retrieval-augmented prompts, median latency ~85ms on Hosted (p95 ~210ms).
- Option 2 — OpenX-13B (FP16): higher quality on long-context summarization, p95 ~320ms on Hosted, better instruction finetune results but ~2.4x cost vs Option 1.
- Option 3 — Redwood-3x-8B (mixed-kernel): compromise option — near OpenX quality on short answers, p95 ~180ms, cost ~1.5x Option 1.

Why these three: we prioritized your two stated constraints from the call — (1) sub-300ms typical latency for chat flows and (2) predictable unit economics for high-throughput customer support scenarios. Option 1 maximizes throughput/cost. Option 2 gives the best quality for long-form summarization and hallucination reduction. Option 3 is a middle path for mixed workloads.

Attachments & links: attached is a small benchmark CSV with the demo prompts we ran (stratus_benchmarks_20270531.csv) and the prompt_set_v1.txt we used. Also included a short playbook PDF that maps run configurations to likely unit costs. Drive + HubSpot links below.

Recommended next steps (proposed cadence):
1) You pick 1–2 models from the shortlist to pilot (we recommend Options 1 + 2 for parallel A/B on the two primary flows).
2) We run a 3-day precision/latency sprint on your sample prompts (we need the ~200 example records you referenced).
3) Redwood provides a concise cost/latency report and suggested quantization/deployment options (Hosted vs Dedicated).
4) Decide on SOW and kickoff (we can scope a minimal pilot SOW within 5 business days).

Open questions we noted on the call:
- exact throughput targets (rps) for peak windows
- retention/security controls required for audit log exports

Please confirm which models you want to pilot and if you can share the 200-sample eval set this week. Happy to hop on a 20-min sync if you prefer.

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
sean@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0182

Alex — thanks, great questions. Quick answers and attached cost sketch: 

1) Rough cost estimates (ballpark, per 1M input+output tokens):
- Option 1 (Redwood-3q-8B, quantized) — Hosted: $220 / 1M tokens; Dedicated (reserved pool): ~$150 / 1M tokens (depends on commit).
- Option 2 (OpenX-13B, FP16) — Hosted: $520 / 1M tokens; Dedicated: ~$320 / 1M tokens.
- Option 3 (Redwood-3x-8B) — Hosted: $330 / 1M tokens; Dedicated: ~$210 / 1M tokens.

Notes on latency SLOs: p95 numbers from our demo cluster (same region) are in the CSV; on Dedicated with burst configuration you can expect ~25–40% improvement on p95 versus Hosted for Options 1 & 3, and ~15–25% improvement for Option 2 depending on batch size. We can include exact p95/p99 scenarios in the pilot report.

2) Regression monitoring / rollback approach:
- We recommend a two-pronged guardrail: continuous evaluation against a fixed prompt set (we'll use your 200 examples + a Redwood regression pack) and production sampling with metric thresholds (answer divergence, hallucination score, user-surveyed quality).
- Canary & automatic fallback: Redwood supports canary rollouts and automatic fallback rules to a pinned previous model variant if regression thresholds are exceeded.
- Auditability: all inference requests can be logged (if you enable audit export) for offline analysis; we support redaction hooks and KMS for keys.

3) Data sharing: please redact account numbers and full SSNs. Our suggested minimal redaction script is in the Drive folder. If you prefer, we can run the first pass inside your VPC (Private) and avoid sending examples off-network.

Attached for reference: cost_sketch_20270531.xlsx (stub) and the prompt_set_v1.txt we used.

Next steps: once you drop the 200 samples we'll schedule the eval sprint (3 business days) and aim to deliver the pilot report within 5 business days after the sprint. I'll draft an SOW outline and share for review in the morning.

Best,
Sean

Attachments referenced: prompt_set_v1.txt, stratus_benchmarks_20270531.csv, redwood_reco_playbook.pdf
